for_senior_author: cl_aya_ceremony_setting, fasting and other ceremony practices (editor's lead). My reading of Perkins et al.: the survey cannot show that fasting, preparation or any ceremony practice changes anything. All features and outcomes were rated by the same self-selected people at one sitting, looking back, with nothing measured before ayahuasca. Fasting was a yes-or-no support offered at the place of drinking. It showed no detectable difference in fear, later difficulties or current distress, but the intervals do not rule out small differences either way (fear −0.29 to 0.15 points on 0 to 10). Its only links were small rises in recalled mystical-orientation scores (1.7 of an 81-point range) and in perceived growth. Support and safety, and preparation for later difficulties, were the only consistent associations, all small (under 2 Kessler points across a whole rating). Decision needed: the SIMO measures the intensity of mystical experience, so reporting fasting's link with it may touch the rule 'nothing on making a drug's effects stronger'. Keep it in the full statement as a recalled association (current text, and kept out of the plain line), or drop it?

cl_xc_mindset_before, status. 'Replicated' now rests only on the anxiety direction: more anxiety before the drug, alone or inside a worse overall state of mind, went with a more anxious or challenging experience in Haijen et al. (set component) and Vizeli et al. (pre-dose anxiety), and in recalled attributions in Simonsson et al. That a better mood goes with an easier experience rests on Haijen alone, because in the Basel laboratory data a better mood went with stronger effects overall. The strict alternative is 'single study' for the claim's opening sentence. The short plain line now leads with what both teams found. Confirm the status, or take the strict reading.

cl_xc_setting_support, status and one added clause. 'Mixed' is kept because the findings differ by aspect: support and safety went with fewer difficulties in two independent retrospective surveys, while blaming the people around (panel) and a retreat or therapeutic setting (prospective) showed no association. 'Replicated' for support and safety alone would also fit §6.4. Haijen's setting rating went with slightly higher well-being two weeks later (p = 0.037, one of 57 uncorrected coefficients). It was added for balance with a new anchor. Keep it or drop it?

The claims now say 'the only prospective study ... among these sources' instead of 'the one prospective study'. Later prospective studies of set and setting in naturalistic use may exist. They were not searched in this round; a targeted search is worth doing before any page calls Haijen et al. the only one.

cl_xc_difficult_how_common carries the lithium and mood-stabilizer signal from 8 and 16 people. The claim writer flagged a missing interactions claim on lithium with psychedelics. Should a separate interactions claim be commissioned (with its own sources on seizures, which this survey did not measure)?

Two new anchors enter as ai-located and need a fresh targeted check before these claims can be ai-anchored: cl_xc_setting_support (Haijen Table 6, setting rows) and cl_aya_ceremony_setting (Perkins Tables 4 and 5, fasting rows). Five wording corrections were made to ai-checked anchors (cl_xc_mindset_before 5, 11, 13; cl_xc_setting_support 2; cl_aya_ceremony_setting 5 locator). Each follows a second reader's note at the stated place and adds no new numbers, except anchor 2's correction of the retreat item's structure, which the blind second reader found. A fresh check of anchor 2 may be preferred.
No risk-of-bias domain or interpretation-gap disagreement remains on the four cards: the second readers agreed with every overall judgment and gap rating.
